dimensions.assessment: The bill directly affects federal agencies, emergency managers, researchers, academic institutions, commercial weather enterprises, and indirectly the entire U.S. population relying on weather forecasts, warnings, and hazard mitigation.

Changes are major and life-changing regarding public safety infrastructure, severe weather warnings, wildfire and flood risk reduction, and commercial data integration, alongside multi-million dollar grant programs.

The bill authorizes significant appropriations across multiple programs and fiscal years, including specific authorizations for weather research, artificial intelligence, NOAA weather radio modernization, and land and water monitoring networks.

The legislation spans twelve distinct titles, creating numerous new programs, interagency councils, pilot projects, testbeds, and statutory amendments to existing laws like the Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Act of 2017.
The provisions establish permanent statutory modifications, multi-year authorizations running through fiscal year 2030 and beyond, and long-term strategic plans and reporting requirements.

missing_information: Total aggregate multi-year appropriations across all titles and programs combined were not explicitly summed in the text.
importance_detail.rationale: S. 3923 reauthorizes and extensively expands federal weather research, forecasting, observation, and hazard communication programs across multiple agencies, particularly NOAA. It authorizes billions of dollars in appropriations across several fiscal years, establishes multiple new interagency councils, testbeds, pilot programs, and grant initiatives, and amends numerous underlying statutes concerning weather, climate, tsunamis, wildfires, and data management.

card.summary: The National Landslide Preparedness Act Reauthorization Act of 2025 reauthorizes and updates federal programs related to landslide hazards, water observation, and data monitoring. It extends funding authorities, incorporates considerations for atmospheric rivers and extreme precipitation events, establishes regional partnerships and new water observation systems, and expands coordination to include Indian tribes, tribal organizations, and Native Hawaiian organizations.

summary: The Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Reauthorization Act of 2026 aims to improve weather research, forecasting, and prediction capabilities at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). It reauthorizes and updates various programs related to severe weather, hurricanes, tsunamis, drought, and fire weather, while also expanding commercial weather data opportunities and artificial intelligence integration.

affected_groups.effect: National Weather Service and NOAA personnel face new training, hiring assessments, shift work health studies, and modernized cloud-based processing systems.
Private entities gain opportunities to contract with NOAA to provide weather data, participate in pilot programs, and access public data repositories.
affected_groups.group: Commercial Weather Enterprises and Private Data Providers

affected_groups.effect: Sectors benefit from improved subseasonal to seasonal forecasts, expanded soil moisture monitoring networks, and enhanced drought information systems.
Residents receive upgraded tsunami warnings, improved flood and precipitation alerts, and better alert parity for remote or isolated areas.

key_provisions: Establishes a Fire Weather Services Program and fire weather testbed to enhance prediction, monitoring, and communication regarding wildfires and smoke.
Updates the Commercial Data Program and Commercial Data Pilot Program to integrate more private sector environmental and weather observations into NOAA models.
Authorizes funds and programs for improving precipitation forecasts, atmospheric river tracking, coastal flooding, and storm surge predictions.
Maintains and modernizes NOAA Weather Radio and establishes standards for flash flood emergency alert systems.
Integrates artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies into advanced computing, weather modeling, and data assimilation.
missing_information: Exact overall mandatory spending amounts outside of specific authorizations provided in various titles are not fully detailed.
Long-term economic impacts on private market competitors are not quantified.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Reauthorization Act of 2026 aims to improve weather research, forecasting, and prediction capabilities at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). It reauthorizes and updates various programs related to severe weather, hurricanes, tsunamis, drought, and fire weather, while also expanding commercial weather data opportunities and artificial intelligence integration.
summary_detail.significance: This bill significantly directs federal weather policy, resource allocation, and technological modernization for NOAA and related agencies through fiscal year 2030, substantially changing how weather data is collected, processed, and communicated to the public.
